utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi Priya. Come on in. How have you been?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I've been okay. I've been thinking a lot about what things would be like if I just wasn't around. Like picturing my funeral, who would come, what they would say. Is that weird?

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: People sometimes think about mortality when they're going through transitions. Have you had any big life changes lately?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Not really. I've just been giving away some of my things. Like I gave my best friend my mom's old jewelry because I thought she'd appreciate it more than I do.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That's a generous gesture. Giving things away can be meaningful. How is your friendship with her going?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: She's great. I wrote her a letter too actually, just telling her how much she means to me and how I'm grateful for everything she's done. I've been writing letters to a few people.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you're reflecting on your relationships. What brought that on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I don't know, I guess I just wanted people to know. Just in case. You never know when your time is up, right? I've just been trying to get things in order.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That's a very mature perspective, thinking about legacy. Is there anything specific that's been worrying you about the future?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: No, nothing specific. I've actually felt very calm and peaceful lately. More than I have in years. I feel like I've finally made peace with things.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That's wonderful to hear. Calm and acceptance are signs of real progress. I'm glad the therapy is helping.
